title: Prefill/Decode: granular phase-throttling and proportional fairness policy
creator: Maya Chen
description: Introduce a scheduler policy that divides prefill/decode work into small, deterministic micro-phases and applies proportional fairness with smoothing to reduce tail latency for short sessions while maintaining throughput for long-running decodes.
motivation: Current hybrid prefill-decode schedulers either favor throughput (large phases, longer batching windows) or favor low tail latency (aggressive splitting) but do not provide a tunable middle path that degrades gracefully. We see customer complaints about interactive requests (chat, assist) getting delayed under mixed workloads when large batched prefill jobs dominate. We need a policy that (1) preserves high aggregate throughput for bulk workloads, (2) provides strong latency fairness for interactive requests, and (3) is safe to rollout incrementally.
proposed_solution:
Design and implement a 'granular phase-throttling' policy. Key ideas:
- Split prefill into micro-phases (~4-16 tokens per micro-phase) for short-session requests; long sessions can aggregate micro-phases to amortize kernel overhead.
- Maintain a per-worker proportional fairness score that tracks recent service time normalized by request priority and token count. Use exponential smoothing (alpha configurable) to compute a smoothed fairness weight.
- Scheduler chooses the next micro-phase across prefill and decode based on min(cost/weight), where cost is an estimate of remaining GPU time for that micro-phase.
- Provide two modes: conservative (favor throughput) and interactive (favor latency) toggled by route-level policy.
- Add fast preemption hooks so a high-priority interactive micro-phase can preempt a queued bulk micro-phase within a configurable budget to avoid starvation.
- Expose configuration knobs in console and as request-level hints: target_p99_latency_ms, fairness_alpha, micro_phase_size_tokens, preempt_budget_ms.
- Integrate metrics and tracing to diagnose fairness violations and throughput regressions.
acceptance_criteria: Scheduler implements micro-phase concept and scheduling decision described above in runtime
Route-level policy exposes interactive vs conservative modes and knobs in config API
Benchmarks show p99 latency for 8-token interactive sessions improves by >= 25% under mixed load compared to current baseline, while aggregate throughput regression is <= 5% for bulk workloads
No observed starvation: 99.99% of requests make forward progress within configured SLA window in mixed workloads
End-to-end integration tests for preemption, fairness smoothing, and config toggles are added to CI
Telemetry dashboards ingest new metrics and show fairness_score, micro_phase_wait_time, preempt_count per-worker
risks: Microsplitting increases kernel launch overhead and may hurt throughput on small-models/hardware if micro_phase_size is too small
Incorrect cost estimation for micro-phase runtime could oscillate scheduling decisions and produce instability
Preemption adds complexity and potential for increased context-switch overhead on GPU workers
Exposing knobs increases configuration surface and may lead to misconfiguration by users (document defaults clearly)
rollout_plan: 1) Implement feature behind runtime flag and a server-side feature-gate
2) Unit + integration tests in CI, measure overhead on microbench infra
3) Canary rollout to internal dev account with low-traffic dedicated cluster for 48h
4) Collect metrics: p50/p95/p99 latency by route, throughput, preempt_count, micro_phase_size distribution
5) Open beta for selected customers with manual opt-in and runtime metrics dashboard
6) Gradual 5% -> 25% -> 100% rollout per region contingent on regression thresholds
metrics: p50/p95/p99 latency by route (prefill vs decode)
aggregate tokens/sec and per-worker GPU occupancy
fairness_score distribution across requests and workers
dependencies: kernel-selection: need access to faster kernel-launch path optimizations (infra change ticket TBD)
observability: new metrics pipeline and console charts (dashboard-2026.02)
design: UX for route-level toggles in Console
tests: microbench: synthetic mixed workload (50% interactive 8-token sessions, 50% bulk 1024-token prefill) comparing baseline vs granular-phase policy
long-run stability: 24-hour soak with mixed load at 80% capacity
fault-injection: simulate incorrect cost-estimates and validate scheduler stability
policy toggle tests: conservative vs interactive mode behavior verification
implementation_notes: Prefer a pure user-space scheduler change with minimal kernel/runtime modifications initially to reduce coupling
Cost estimator should leverage existing attention-cost models (attention ops scale with seq^2 for prefill) and emit per-micro-phase estimates
Smoothing alpha default = 0.2 (configurable); choose window to balance reactivity and noise
Keep fast-path for single-micro-phase urgent requests to minimize added latency for low-overhead flows
Document default micro_phase_size_tokens=8 and provide guidance for model families and hardware types
